description: AUTOINCREMENT / IDENTITY column forms: word seeds (START n, INCREMENT n, in any order, with ORDER/NOORDER parsed), the (start, step) paren form, negative increments counting down, plain AUTOINCREMENT defaulting to (1,1), and IDENTITY(start, step) surviving a table-level PRIMARY KEY. Two-single-INSERT tests skip snowflake (a NOORDER column allocates in nondeterministic batches per statement there - the Java tests carried the same assumption); multi-row single INSERTs are contiguous and run everywhere. Converted 1:1 from ddl/IdentityColumnFormsTest and IdentityWithPrimaryKeyTest (both now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE w1 (id INT AUTOINCREMENT START 10, n VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO w1 (n) VALUES ('a'), ('b')
SELECT id FROM w1 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE w2 (id INT AUTOINCREMENT INCREMENT 2, n VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO w2 (n) VALUES ('a'), ('b')
SELECT id FROM w2 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE w3 (id INT AUTOINCREMENT INCREMENT 2 START 10 NOORDER, n VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO w3 (n) VALUES ('a'), ('b')
SELECT id FROM w3 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE w4 (id INT AUTOINCREMENT START 10 ORDER, n VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO w4 (n) VALUES ('a')
SELECT id FROM w4
CREATE TABLE wneg (id BIGINT AUTOINCREMENT INCREMENT -1, n VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO wneg (n) VALUES ('a'), ('b')
SELECT id FROM wneg ORDER BY id DESC

skip.reason: a NOORDER autoincrement allocates in nondeterministic per-statement batches on a real account (Java test had the same assumption); Frostlake models the gapless allocation
